acceptanceCriteria.title: With "Most prompts" selected, the cards are in descending order of the prompt count shown on them.
The count on a card equals the number of prompts listed in its panel.
The default sort and the export are unchanged when the option is not selected.

requirements: We should add a sort option "Most prompts" on the Target Sources list. The current sort (failing articles) stays the default.
The sort applies within the current tab (All, Improve visibility, Improve perception) and the current scope and period, the same way the default sort does today (10.6).
Each card shows the number of prompts that use the source, eg: "Used in 24 prompts".

The count is the number of distinct prompts whose answers cite the domain in the period, all LLMs and locales together. It is NOT qualifyingAnswerCitations, which counts answers (one prompt gives several answers across LLMs and runs). It must match the count in the "Prompts associated with this source" section of the panel.
Ties are sorted by failing articles, then domain.
technicalNotes: Current sort: failing articles, then badges, then citations, then domain (TargetSourcesService.java:274 on developer)
Count is NOT qualifyingAnswerCitations (counts answers, not distinct prompts)

acceptanceCriteria.title: A page whose verdict was confirmed by a capture less than N days ago is not captured again: its existing verdict is reused. Proposed N: 3 days, pending PM confirmation.
acceptanceCriteria.note: No formal AC section in Jira; taken from the "Expected" section

technicalNotes: PR (draft): https://github.com/AirPR/geo-analytics/pull/867 — geo-backend only, the Actions Center job is not touched
N is a setting, it can change without a release
A reuse never counts as a capture: every page is read again at least every N days
Reuse = no Firecrawl capture and no AI judge call
Above 7 days nothing more is saved (a verdict is judged again every 7 days anyway)
